summary: File gə-mʕambrí-way-na under Infectum-wa and the container-filling construction.
rationale: Explicit -way-na marks the past habitual form. Bare aʕ=ʕanēbrayḏan and zād encode container and material; the same quotation is already present with an editorial government note.

summary: Move the -way-na example from Infectum to Infectum-wa.
rationale: The quoted verb gə-mʕambrí-way-na contains the past habitual -way-na ending. The supplied JL 13.12/13 confirms gəmʕambriwayna, and the translation is past (“wir füllten”). Both form and context establish Infectum-wa rather than unmarked Infectum.

summary: New sense 1a: Speicher mit Getreide füllen
rationale: Container and material both appear as bare nominal groups, contrasting with stored grain plus b-marked storage location in the inherited Preterit. The existing example supports the construction.

summary: The denominal storage verb alternates between a stored-theme object plus b-marked storehouse (PrS 8/19) and a bare container plus bare material (JL 13.12/13). The lettered construction records that valency difference without changing the inherited store sense.
The entry’s explicit government note already flags JL 13.12.13 as interesting. Its form is not a new attestation: only its box and constructional sense assignment change.
gəmʕambriwayna is Infectum-wa, with habitual past -wayna. The bare Infectum label in the source entry is a filing error.
Keep the glossary’s inherited stem label I and denominal etymological note. The quadriliteral root shape does not by itself authorise changing the team’s stem taxonomy.
The mʕamballe wheat-storage example is identical to the inherited prs 19/16 quotation; supplied PrS 8/19 is a numbering-concordance issue, not another example.
Verify the edition concordance between prs 19/16 and supplied PrS 8/19 before replacing the inherited reference.
How productive is the bare container plus bare material construction beyond granaries and grain? Only one such attestation is supplied, so the new subsense makes no broader productivity claim.
